extracted.intended_audience: Interested public, stakeholders, licensees, design vendors, and other persons who may submit comments on the NRC proposed rule (NRC-2025-0018)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for obtaining information, submitting public comments, and understanding what constitutes a significant adverse comment for the Nuclear Regulatory Commission proposed rule revising the duration of design certifications (Docket NRC-2025-0018).

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments deadline / timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit comments on the proposed rule by August 1, 2025. Comments received after this date will be considered if it is practical to do so, but the NRC is able to ensure consideration only for comments received on or before this date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Late comments may be considered at NRC discretion but are not guaranteed to be considered; include the docket ID when submitting so comments are associated with the rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to submit comments (preferred methods and contact info)
rubrics_metrics.description: The NRC encourages electronic comment submission through the Federal rulemaking website (https://www.regulations.gov) by searching for Docket ID NRC-2025-0018.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other methods: email to Rulemaking.Comments@nrc.gov; fax to Secretary, U.S. NRC at 301-415-1101; mail to Secretary, U.S. NRC, Washington, DC 20555-0001, ATTN: Rulemakings and Adjudications Staff; hand deliver to 11555 Rockville Pike, Rockville, Maryland between 7:30 a.m. and 4:15 p.m. ET, Federal workdays. If you do not receive an automatic email reply confirming receipt, contact 301-415-1677. Include Docket ID NRC-2025-0018 in your submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not include identifying/contact information you do not want publicly disclosed
rubrics_metrics.description: The NRC cautions you not to include identifying or contact information that you do not want to be publicly disclosed in your comment submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NRC will post all comment submissions to https://www.regulations.gov and enter them into ADAMS and does not routinely edit comment submissions to remove identifying or contact information. If aggregating comments, inform contributors not to include identifying/contact information they do not want publicly disclosed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a 'significant adverse comment'
rubrics_metrics.description: A significant adverse comment is a comment where the commenter explains why the rule would be inappropriate, including challenges to the rule's underlying premise or approach, or would be ineffective or unacceptable without a change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A comment is adverse and significant if it meets any of the following: (1) It opposes the rule and provides a reason sufficient to require a substantive response in a notice-and-comment process (examples: (a) causes NRC staff to reevaluate or conduct additional analysis; (b) raises an issue serious enough to warrant a substantive response to clarify or complete the record; (c) raises a relevant issue not previously addressed); (2) It proposes a change or addition to the rule, and it is apparent the rule would be ineffective or unacceptable without incorporation of the change; (3) It causes the NRC staff to make a change (other than editorial) to the rule. Receipt of significant adverse comments by the deadline will cause withdrawal of the direct final rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct final rule procedure and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Because NRC considers this action non-controversial, it is publishing the proposed rule concurrently with a direct final rule. The direct final rule will become effective on September 15, 2025, unless significant adverse comments are received by August 1, 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If significant adverse comments are received by the deadline, NRC will publish a document withdrawing the direct final rule and will address the comments in a subsequent final rule or as otherwise appropriate. Absent significant modifications requiring republication, NRC will not initiate a second comment period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment content that triggers substantive agency response
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of comment content that would require a substantive response include causing NRC staff to reevaluate its position or conduct additional analysis; raising an issue serious enough to warrant substantive response to clarify or complete the record; or raising a relevant issue not previously addressed by NRC staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To be considered significant adverse, a comment should explain why the rule is inappropriate or ineffective without change, propose a necessary change, or otherwise prompt non-editorial change by the staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to include Docket ID in submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Please refer to Docket ID NRC-2025-0018 when contacting NRC about the availability of information and include Docket ID NRC-2025-0018 in your comment submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including the docket ID ensures your submission is associated with this rulemaking and retrievable via regulations.gov and NRC docket systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of materials and how to obtain them
rubrics_metrics.description: Publicly available information related to this action may be obtained via regulations.gov (Docket ID NRC-2025-0018), NRC's ADAMS Public Documents collection, the NRC Public Document Room (PDR), and the NRC Technical Library.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ADAMS: select 'Begin Web-based ADAMS Search' and use accession numbers provided; PDR and Technical Library are open by appointment and provide contact emails and phone numbers for assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and substance of the proposed regulatory change (DC duration)
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule would replace the 15-year duration period for initial design certifications (DCs) and renewals with a 40-year duration period, both generically and for each DC currently in effect. This proposed rule would not change the date of issuance or renewal for existing DCs (i.e., the start date remains unchanged).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For appendix D (AP1000), the rule would replace the existing 20-year duration with 40 years. The change applies to the five DCs currently in effect and does not apply to two expired DCs (appendices B and C). The 40-year period starts upon the date of issuance or renewal of the DC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationale for change and safety/security assurances
rubrics_metrics.description: NRC proposes the change based on lessons learned from the DC renewal process: the 15-year period did not allow sufficient time for operating experience to accumulate prior to expiration/renewal, creating unnecessary burdens. Other regulations and processes will continue to ensure safety and security.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission may modify, rescind, or impose new requirements under § 52.63(a)(1) when necessary to provide adequate protection of public health and safety or common defense and security. Plant-specific orders, departure processes in DC appendices, and petitions for rulemaking provide mechanisms to address safety or security issues post-certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship to other regulatory processes (modifications, departures, petitions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Existing regulations provide criteria and mechanisms for making changes to DC rules, including § 52.63(a)(1) for Commission action, petitions for rulemaking, plant-specific orders, and the departure process in DC appendices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changes to DC rules may be made on the Commission's own motion or in response to petitions and will provide notice and opportunity for public comment. Licensees and applicants referencing a DC may address potential safety/security concerns via the departure process, license amendment, or exemption; NRC will evaluate such requests using typical processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork Reduction Act statement
rubrics_metrics.description: This proposed rule does not contain any new or amended collections of information subject to the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995. Existing collections were approved by OMB, approval number 3150-0151.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public Protection Notification: NRC may not conduct or sponsor, and a person is not required to respond to, a collection of information unless the document requesting the collection displays a currently valid OMB control number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain Writing Act compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The NRC has written this document to be consistent with the Plain Writing Act of 2010 which requires Federal agencies to write documents in a clear, concise, and well-organized manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The document also follows the Presidential Memorandum 'Plain Language in Government Writing' (June 10, 1998). This informs how the NRC frames explanations and instructions for commenters and stakeholders.
